title: New U.S. Sanctions Will Harm Ukraine Peace Talks and Bilateral Ties, Kremlin Says
text: New U.S. Sanctions Will Harm Ukraine Peace Talks and Bilateral Ties, Kremlin Says Sep. 21, 2026 Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. Sputnik / Alexander Kazakov / Reuters U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to sign a law expanding sanctions on Russia will hinder efforts to end the war in Ukraine and further damage relations between Moscow and Washington , the Kremlin said Monday. “The signing of this document is certainly something that doesn’t contribute to the resuscitation of our bilateral relations,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a daily briefing. “ It is also of course unlikely to contribute to more successful progress along the path toward a settlement in Ukraine,” Peskov said. The law, which Trump signed Friday, authorizes the U.S. president to impose punitive tariffs of up to 100% on China, India and other countries over their purchases of Russian oil and gas. text: 17.23 EDT Albanese signs declaration with world leaders urging human control over AI Anthony Albanese has joined the leaders of more than 20 countries in signing a statement calling to bring the rapid growth of artificial intelligence under control. “AI must remain under human direction, oversight and control. It must be developed and used in line with international law,” the statement said. Leading scientists and executives are warning that the pace of development could outpace our ability to manage emerging risks. The Canadian prime minister Mark Carney , the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz , Spain’s PM, Pedro Sánchez , and European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, also signed the statement. “Artificial intelligence has the potential to improve lives, to strengthen our economy and productivity, and to massively advance science and medical breakthroughs,” Albanese said. But humans need to be in control of it. If it’s going to be successful, then we need to make sure that humans are at the centre of everything that occurs. text: ЧЕТЫРЕ ГОДА ВЕРНОСТИ ДОЛГУ Этот ролик посвящается мобилизованным. Тем, кто четыре года назад встал на защиту Отечества и остаётся в строю сегодня. 21 сентября 2022 года привычная жизнь тысяч мужчин разделилась на «до» и «после». Семья, работа, дети, планы — всё пришлось оставить ради военной формы, службы и дороги, которую никто из них заранее для себя не выбирал. Осенью 2022-го каждый принимал своё решение. Пока кто-то искал путь за границу и стоял в очередях на Верхнем Ларсе, они выбрали другую дорогу — в воинскую часть. Не потому, что им нечего было терять. Им было что терять. Но было и что защищать. За четыре года они прошли через бои, потери, бессонные ночи и тяжёлые дороги. Узнали, что такое настоящее боевое братство и сколько иногда значат самые простые слова: «Брат, я рядом». Они разные. Из разных городов и народов огромной страны. Кто-то православный, кто-то мусульманин, кто-то следует другой вере. Каждый обращается к Богу по-своему, но перед боевой задачей молитвы звучат об одном — сберечь товарищей, выполнить долг и вернуться к своим. Сегодня слово «мобилизованный» уже не может рассказать о них главное. Это воины. Это защитники. Это герои нашего времени. Родина для них —
author: Boris Rozhin

title: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst
text: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst By Leyla Latypova and Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 21, 2026 A man boards a bus in Moscow during Russia's "partial" mobilization in September 2022. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Rumors that the Kremlin could order another mobilization to sustain its invasion of Ukraine after this month’s parliamentary elections have circulated in Russian media for months. Now that the ruling, pro-Kremlin United Russia party has secured a record majority, anti-war activists and lawyers told The Moscow Times that anxiety is rising, even though helping Russians avoid military service has long been a routine part of their work. When the Kremlin called up 300,000 reservists in September 2022 in Russia’s first mobilization since World War II, the announcement sparked an exodus of tens of thousands of Russians and protests in dozens of cities. At least 20,468 of the men who were mobilized in 2022 were confirmed killed as of this month, according to an independent tally. Activists told The Moscow Times that the renewed speculation about another mobilization “echoes with pain” — and that a new call-up could be faster

title: United Russia Set for Record Parliament Majority in First Wartime Elections
text: United Russia Set for Record Parliament Majority in First Wartime Elections Sep. 21, 2026 Former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and other Russian officials celebrate United Russia's electoral victory. Sputnik / Yekaterina Shtukina / Reuters Russia’s ruling party, United Russia, is on track to secure a record number of seats in the lower-house State Duma following the country's first parliamentary elections since the launch of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, preliminary results showed Monday. With 95% of the ballots counted, Central Election Commission (CEC) chief Ella Pamfilova announced that United Russia received 57.83% of the party-list vote while dominating single-member districts, where its candidates were leading in 208 of 225 constituencies. Pamfilova said United Russia stands to capture around 355 seats in the 450-seat State Duma — surpassing its previous record of 343 seats set in 2016 and comfortably maintaining its constitutional supermajority. Four other parties cleared the threshold to enter parliament: the Communist Party with 40 seats, the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) with 25, New People with 20 and A Just Russia

Source: Oleksandr Vilkul , Head of Kryvyi Rih Defence Council; Ukraine's Air Force , Oleksandr Hanzha , Head of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration; monitoring Telegram channels Details: Hanzha said that Russian forces had simultaneously struck industrial facilities in three cities in the oblast. title: Russia launches largest oil mega-project since Soviet era in Taimyr – photos
text: Russia launches largest oil mega-project since Soviet era in Taimyr – photos Ivan Diakonov — 22 September, 01:55 Stock photo: Getty Images Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google Russia has begun commercial oil exports from V ostok Oi l, the country's largest group of oilfields developed since the collapse of the Soviet Union, sending the first shipments of crude to Asia aboard ice-class tankers via the Northern Sea Route. Source: The Moscow Times Details: Rosneft, Russia 's state-controlled oil giant , has begun loading four specialised ice-class tankers at the Bukhta Sever terminal. title: Zelenskyy meets CIA chief in Ireland – Reuters
text: Zelenskyy meets CIA chief in Ireland – Reuters Tetyana Oliynyk — 21 September, 23:24 Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Photo: Getty Images Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has met CIA Director John Ratcliffe at Shannon Airport in Ireland. Source: Reuters , citing two sources familiar with the meeting Details: One source said that the meeting had taken place on 21 September. Advertisement: Another source stated that the two had spoken while their aircraft were refuelling, without specifying the exact date. Both sources declined to disclose details of the conversation. Background: On 25 August, it was reported that the CIA director had visited Moscow . On 28 August, Zelenskyy thanked the US side for the necessary "tone of the conversation with Russia". title: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst
text: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst By Leyla Latypova and Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 21, 2026 A man boards a bus in Moscow during Russia's "partial" mobilization in September 2022. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Rumors that the Kremlin could order another mobilization to sustain its invasion of Ukraine after this month’s parliamentary elections have circulated in Russian media for months. Now that the ruling, pro-Kremlin United Russia party has secured a record majority, anti-war activists and lawyers told The Moscow Times that anxiety is rising, even though helping Russians avoid military service has long been a routine part of their work. When the Kremlin called up 300,000 reservists in September 2022 in Russia’s first mobilization since World War II, the announcement sparked an exodus of tens of thousands of Russians and protests in dozens of cities. At least 20,468 of the men who were mobilized in 2022 were confirmed killed as of this month, according to an independent tally. Activists told The Moscow Times that the renewed speculation about another mobilization “echoes with pain” — and that a new call-up could be faster

title: Russian-Armenian Relations Will ‘Inevitably Change,’ Pashinyan Says
text: Russian-Armenian Relations Will ‘Inevitably Change,’ Pashinyan Says Sep. 21, 2026 Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. Sputnik / Petr Kovalev / Reuters Relations between Russia and Armenia are bound to shift regardless of who holds power in Yerevan, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said , as his country gradually normalizes ties with Azerbaijan and moves closer to Europe. “Our relations with Russia will inevitably change. This is not connected to any individual or political force. Whoever it may be, Armenia-Russia relations will not be the same as before,” Pashinyan said in an interview published this weekend. He said bilateral ties “cannot remain the same as long as there is an environment of peace in Armenia.” Tensions between traditional allies Russia and Armenia have grown since Azerbaijan regained control of the breakaway region of Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023. Armenia accused Russia and its peacekeeping forces of failing to deter Baku’s military offensive. “Armenia-Russia relations under conditions of conflict are one thing, while Armenia-Russia relations under conditions of peace are another,” Pashinyan told Boon TV. news Armenia's Pashinyan Asks Putin to Help Resolve

title: United Russia Set for Record Parliament Majority in First Wartime Elections
text: United Russia Set for Record Parliament Majority in First Wartime Elections Sep. 21, 2026 Former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and other Russian officials celebrate United Russia's electoral victory. Sputnik / Yekaterina Shtukina / Reuters Russia’s ruling party, United Russia, is on track to secure a record number of seats in the lower-house State Duma following the country's first parliamentary elections since the launch of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, preliminary results showed Monday. With 95% of the ballots counted, Central Election Commission (CEC) chief Ella Pamfilova announced that United Russia received 57.83% of the party-list vote while dominating single-member districts, where its candidates were leading in 208 of 225 constituencies. Pamfilova said United Russia stands to capture around 355 seats in the 450-seat State Duma — surpassing its previous record of 343 seats set in 2016 and comfortably maintaining its constitutional supermajority. Four other parties cleared the threshold to enter parliament: the Communist Party with 40 seats, the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) with 25, New People with 20 and A Just Russia

A total of 285 objects ranging from straw hats to sunglasses and nightgowns to tableware and furniture from La Madrague and La Garrigue, Bardot's homes in Saint-Tropez in southeastern France, as well as her Paris apartment generated tremendous enthusiasm, an AFP journalist said. Sputnik / Yekaterina Shtukina / Reuters Russia’s ruling party, United Russia, is on track to secure a record number of seats in the lower-house State Duma following the country's first parliamentary elections since the launch of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, preliminary results showed Monday. With 95% of the ballots counted, Central Election Commission (CEC) chief Ella Pamfilova announced that United Russia received 57.83% of the party-list vote while dominating single-member districts, where its candidates were leading in 208 of 225 constituencies. Pamfilova said United Russia stands to capture around 355 seats in the 450-seat State Duma — surpassing its previous record of 343 seats set in 2016 and comfortably maintaining its constitutional supermajority. Four other parties cleared the threshold to enter parliament: the Communist Party with 40 seats, the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) with 25, New People with 20 and A Just Russia

title: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst
text: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst By Leyla Latypova and Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 21, 2026 A man boards a bus in Moscow during Russia's "partial" mobilization in September 2022. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Rumors that the Kremlin could order another mobilization to sustain its invasion of Ukraine after this month’s parliamentary elections have circulated in Russian media for months. Now that the ruling, pro-Kremlin United Russia party has secured a record majority, anti-war activists and lawyers told The Moscow Times that anxiety is rising, even though helping Russians avoid military service has long been a routine part of their work. When the Kremlin called up 300,000 reservists in September 2022 in Russia’s first mobilization since World War II, the announcement sparked an exodus of tens of thousands of Russians and protests in dozens of cities. At least 20,468 of the men who were mobilized in 2022 were confirmed killed as of this month, according to an independent tally. Activists told The Moscow Times that the renewed speculation about another mobilization “echoes with pain” — and that a new call-up could be faster

title: Russian-Armenian Relations Will ‘Inevitably Change,’ Pashinyan Says
text: Russian-Armenian Relations Will ‘Inevitably Change,’ Pashinyan Says Sep. 21, 2026 Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. Sputnik / Petr Kovalev / Reuters Relations between Russia and Armenia are bound to shift regardless of who holds power in Yerevan, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said , as his country gradually normalizes ties with Azerbaijan and moves closer to Europe. “Our relations with Russia will inevitably change. This is not connected to any individual or political force. Whoever it may be, Armenia-Russia relations will not be the same as before,” Pashinyan said in an interview published this weekend. He said bilateral ties “cannot remain the same as long as there is an environment of peace in Armenia.” Tensions between traditional allies Russia and Armenia have grown since Azerbaijan regained control of the breakaway region of Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023. Armenia accused Russia and its peacekeeping forces of failing to deter Baku’s military offensive. “Armenia-Russia relations under conditions of conflict are one thing, while Armenia-Russia relations under conditions of peace are another,” Pashinyan told Boon TV. news Armenia's Pashinyan Asks Putin to Help Resolve

title: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst
text: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst By Leyla Latypova and Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 21, 2026 A man boards a bus in Moscow during Russia's "partial" mobilization in September 2022. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Rumors that the Kremlin could order another mobilization to sustain its invasion of Ukraine after this month’s parliamentary elections have circulated in Russian media for months. Now that the ruling, pro-Kremlin United Russia party has secured a record majority, anti-war activists and lawyers told The Moscow Times that anxiety is rising, even though helping Russians avoid military service has long been a routine part of their work. When the Kremlin called up 300,000 reservists in September 2022 in Russia’s first mobilization since World War II, the announcement sparked an exodus of tens of thousands of Russians and protests in dozens of cities. At least 20,468 of the men who were mobilized in 2022 were confirmed killed as of this month, according to an independent tally. Activists told The Moscow Times that the renewed speculation about another mobilization “echoes with pain” — and that a new call-up could be faster
